1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 c5 5. Nb5 Na6 6. c3 Bd7 7. a4 Be7 8. Bd3 c4 9. Bb1
comments.comment:
On b1 rather than c2: here the bishop shuts the first rank, and that decides the a-file fight after ...Bxb5 (see 11.b6). It has one downside: it also cuts our a1-rook off from the queen. So against ...Qa5 the bishop goes back to c2, and ...Bxb5 axb5 then opens the a-file against the black queen: (9... Qa5 10. Bc2 Bxb5 11. axb5)
Against ...Qb6, develop with Nf3: (9... Qb6 10. Nf3)

comments.comment: If the knight goes back to b8 instead, just develop: (10... Nb8 11. Nf3)

comments.comment: The point of Bb1: if Black takes, Bxc7 wins, because ...Rxa1 no longer hits our queen. Against ...Na6, take on a7: (11... Na6 12. bxa7)
